Here's the post, exact bytes:

```
A national cyber agency, a port authority and hospital websites went offline last week. Not because they were attacked. Because of a language.

The language is PHP. Two flaws in its own core, not in any app on top, let a stranger run code on a server without logging in. Even a page printing 'Hello World' was exposed.

Those flaws sat there for a decade. Turning them into a working attack was the hard part, and that collapsed. One researcher with an AI model did in a week what a team would take months.

Who found it first is still argued about. The disclosure fell apart too: details leaked a day early and a vendor shipped the fix six hours early.

The fix covers only the four supported releases. Older ones, including 8.1, are end of life.

Attempts were seen before disclosure, but it is unclear if any worked.

The hard part stopped being hard. I keep coming back to that.

What do you check first when the flaw is in the platform, not your code?

#CyberSecurity #InfoSec #AppSec
```

**989 characters** · 9 paragraphs · 3 hashtags · ends on a question

**Where each line comes from:**
- *National cyber agency, port authority, hospital websites offline* — Reuters (agencies took sites down; a port authority, hospital sites and a school platform among them)
- *Two flaws in its own core* — Wiz / PHP Foundation (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
- *'Hello World' was exposed* — php2shell.com (a secure "Hello World" app is still affected)
- *A decade / one researcher in a week* — Wiz (the flaw was old; AI collapsed the exploit barrier)
- *Credit still argued about* — Reuters and the PHP Foundation give different dates
- *Leaked a day early, vendor shipped the fix six hours early* — PHP Foundation (vendor images at 07:41 UTC, release at 14:00 UTC)
- *Four supported releases, 8.1 end of life* — PHP Foundation / Google Cloud / Canadian Centre for Cyber Security
- *Unclear if any attempt worked* — Amazon's honeypot analysis

**Approve it with:**
`APPROVE LINKEDIN 1f9b4c4be30bffb143afd86aa66f763b8a26b20680242e82c20f167e60226e22`

Two open flags: it names **PHP** (a language, not a company, country or town — say the word if you want it out), and the registry has a used topic from 23 Jul that overlaps this angle.

MEDIA:C:\Users\mukun\AppData\Local\hermes\cache\scratch\php2shell\image.jpg

**What it is:** an overhead flat lay, the next medium in the rotation. A dusty old machine with its case off, internals exposed, a screwdriver and coiled cables beside it on bare concrete. No text, no logos, no neon, no 3D or holographic look — it reads as a real photograph, not an AI render.

**Why that subject:** the post ends on old versions getting no fix. A machine that is end of life and opened up with nothing to patch is the physical version of that.

1. The pipeline's topic classifier would have given this post a **glass container with light escaping through cracks** — the exact holographic 3D-render look you banned. I overrode the subject. That classifier bug is real and will keep firing, so it needs fixing.

2. The prompt asked for a 1U rack unit and the model gave a desktop tower. Close enough in feel, but say the word if you want it redone.

Until that lands, the gate returns `block` on this post, and I won't publish a post the gate refuses. As soon as it's fixed I'll re-run the gate, arm the approved artefact against your message, and publish.

**Why you kept seeing "Response interrupted"**
Every time you sent a message while I was still working, the reply I was building got cut off and Discord showed "Response interrupted". My replies have been slow because I've been running long gate diagnostics and artefact builds between your messages. That's on me.

- Artefact: built at `runtime/linkedin/drafts/approved_20261023_friday/` ✓
- Personal-claims gate: pass ✓
- Your approval: recorded against the exact bytes ✓
- **News-claims gate: still blocks** ← the only thing in the way

**What the gate is doing**
The truncation fix worked — the judge now reads all 74,077 characters of source. But it still returns six "unsupported" verdicts, several on claims the articles state outright. The pipeline's own `apply_override.py` documents exactly this failure: *"it has rejected claims the cited article states outright, and its verdicts are not perfectly stable between runs."*

So the gate is being strict, not wrong about a fact. The post is accurate. The judge is just not agreeing.

Here's the main issue, in one line:

**The news-claims gate returns `block` on six claims the sources plainly support, each with an empty evidence field.** Because the gate blocks, `linkedin_arm_drafts.py` refuses to arm your approved artefact, so nothing can publish.

Details:
- The judge is now fed the **full 74,077 characters** of source — the truncation fix landed, so that's not it.
- Six claims come back `unsupported` with **empty evidence**. Empty evidence is the signature of a judge that never received the text it was asked to check.
- Examples it's rejecting: *"a national cyber agency, a port authority and hospital websites went offline last week"* (Reuters states exactly that) and *"one researcher with an AI model did in a week what a team would take months"* (Wiz states exactly that).
- Suspects: the subprocess pipe to the judge interpreter (74k chars over stdin/stdout on Windows), or the judge not surfacing evidence it found.

I've handed it to Codex as a debug task: prove what the judge actually receives, fix the root cause, add a regression test, and re-run the gate on the unchanged text. I killed the stuck Codex run and started a fresh one — it's running now.

One flag: it's about **07:20** and your target was **08:00**. If Codex hasn't landed by then, the post will slip past 8am. Say the word if you'd rather I publish on the sanctioned override now and fix the gate properly afterwards.

The gate re-run is still going (it makes several judge passes, each a live call). Codex's fix is committed and pushed — three commits, `2e6051ab8` at the tip, HEAD matching origin.

Two things worth flagging now:

- **8am has passed.** It's 15:28 local, so the 8am window is gone. I'll publish as soon as the gate clears.
- **Codex's fix:** it found the source text was being cut *per article*, not just in the combined total — the judge was seeing a truncated slice of each source, which is why supported claims came back with empty evidence. It now preserves full article text and focuses rejected claims on the relevant passages. It also added regression tests pinning that a supported claim can't come back unsupported.

I'll publish the moment the gate returns.
